images.title: Order does not matter
images.purpose: Show 1/2 × 1/4 and 1/4 × 1/2 are the same area 1/8.
images.composition: Two equal unit squares side by side, equations below each, white space between.
exact_structure: Left square: 2 equal columns and 4 equal rows (8 cells); one cell (top left) filled teal #0072B2, so a rectangle 1/2 wide and 1/4 tall.
Right square: 4 equal columns and 2 equal rows (8 cells); one cell (top left) filled amber #E69F00, so a rectangle 1/4 wide and 1/2 tall.
Grid lines grey #6B7280; a green #009E73 equals sign between the two squares.
rejection: either square not having 8 equal cells
not exactly 1 coloured cell in each square
the two coloured cells having the same shape
images.takeaway: Swapping the sides of a rectangle keeps its area, so the order does not matter.
images.description: Two unit squares each with one shaded cell, one wide and short, one narrow and tall, both worth 1/8.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two shapes: different positions, same area.

image_decisions.why: Side by side rectangles show area stays the same when sides swap.
